Extra prose terms: 'Strictly forbidden to use for impersonation, fraud, or disinformation. AI-generated content should be clearly labeled.' candidates.artificial_voice_method: Voice design from text description, native to V2 only: put the description in parentheses at the start of the text, e.g. text='(A young woman, gentle and sweet voice)Hello...' (card + https://voxcpm.readthedocs.io/en/latest/usage_guide.html). Description covers gender, age, tone, emotion, pace; English and Chinese instructions; no reference audio. Also the 'voxcpm design' CLI. Without any description or reference, the model makes a random voice each call.
candidates.voice_consistency: Design alone is NOT stable: usage guide says with no reference audio 'VoxCPM generates a random voice each time ... timbre will not stay consistent across calls'; cookbook says every generation has 'subtle, unique variations ... like hiring a new voice actor each time'; card says design results 'may vary between runs; generating 1-3 times is recommended'. Docs' own advice for consistency: reuse the same reference audio via reference_wav_path (cloning mode, 5-30 s clip) or LoRA fine-tuning. Workable path from the docs: design once, keep the generated clip, then clone from that model-invented clip for all later text (allowed by rule 2). README examples also pass seed=42 to generate(); no source states that a seed fixes a designed voice across different texts (not tested, no weights run). Style instruction in parentheses can be combined with reference clip.
